comparison: Perfect overlap on therapeutic/clinical speculation claims (C7, C131, C161, C164, C169). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of clinical outcome data and low BKCa-DEC prevalence. Peer reviewers SUPPORT the potential therapeutic relevance as reasonable speculation, acknowledging limitations but not challenging the therapeutic implications.

Both address Ca2+ imaging data (C45-C61, C134-C144). OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with differential paxilline/iberiotoxin sensitivity validating intracellular localization. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, with Reviewer 2 raising critical concerns about calibration methodology and whether comparisons between conditions are valid without proper calibration, though authors added ionomycin calibrations in revision.

Both evaluate nanostring patient expression data (C116-C118, C126-C127, C159-C160). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with clear documentation of prevalence but notes limitations. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the clinical expression data without challenge, though acknowledging limitations regarding hormone receptor-positive cohort and small BKCa-DEC positive sample size.

Both address proliferation assays (C111-C115, C122). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with differential paxilline/iberiotoxin sensitivity and Ki-67 validation addressing MTT concerns. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY: Reviewer 1's specific concern about MTT methodology was addressed by Ki-67 addition, but Reviewer 2's broader concern about attributing effects to mitochondrial versus other intracellular BKCa pools remains.

Both address plasma membrane electrophysiology (C29-C44 overlap). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging electrophysiological and imaging evidence for functional BKCa at plasma membrane. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 2 noting the BK knockout controls as 'a major strength' and experiments as 'astute and well designed.' Plasma membrane data serve as accepted positive controls.

Both evaluate mitoplast patch-clamp evidence (C93-C102). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong electrophysiological identity confirmation, though notes low detection frequencies. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY: while acknowledging 'it is clear these cells have a BK in mitochondria,' Reviewer 2 questions whether metabolic effects can be attributed to this mitochondrial channel versus other intracellular locations. Reviewer 1 questions the surprisingly low mitoplast-positive frequency (6-15%).

Both address mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP measurements (C75-C86, C87-C92, C147-C148). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with consistent paxilline sensitivity supporting intracellular BKCa, though notes ATP-synthase direction inference is indirect. Peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY: Reviewer 1 questions the long time course and overnight preincubation approach, asking why immediate paired experiments weren't performed. Reviewer 2's concern about attribution to mitoBKCa versus other intracellular pools applies.

Both evaluate metabolic flux and lactate data. OpenEval R3 addresses Seahorse/LC-MS data (C62-C74) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 addresses broader metabolic conclusions (C3-C4, C62-C74, C103-C110, C120-C121, C146, C148-C149) as UNCERTAIN. Reviewer 2 explicitly states 'the main conclusion regarding the role of a BK channel located in mitochondria appears is not sufficiently supported,' noting that while intracellular BK effects are 'well substantiated,' linking them specifically to mitochondrial BKCa is not proven.

OpenEval R7 addresses Laconic lactate measurements and Warburg effect (C103-C110, C121, C149) as SUPPORTED with strong isoform-specific and siRNA evidence. Peer R2 includes these claims in broader UNCERTAIN evaluation of metabolic conclusions, with Reviewer 2 noting 'a confounding factor is the likely expression of BK in other intracellular locations such as ER, Golgi, endosomes, etc.'

Both address 2-NBDG glucose uptake data (C87-C92). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with opposite FCCP effects in WT versus BK-KO providing strong evidence, though notes ATP-synthase direction is inferred indirectly. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAINTY evaluation of mitochondrial measurements (R5) applies here, with concerns about whether effects can be specifically attributed to mitoBKCa.

OpenEval R10 addresses main study conclusions (C3-C5, C119-C120, C123-C125, C146, C167-C168) as SUPPORTED with converging multi-method evidence, though notes mitoBKCa as primary mediator is based on localization assumptions. Peer R2 evaluates overlapping metabolic conclusions (C3-C4, C120, C146) as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 stating the mitochondrial attribution 'is not sufficiently supported' despite acknowledging both mitochondrial channel presence and intracellular metabolic effects are individually well-substantiated.

OpenEval R12 addresses background knowledge and prior work citations (C1, C8-C28, C130, C140, C145, C150-C153, C156-C157) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate background/citation claims.

OpenEval R13 addresses study limitations and interpretations (C128-C129, C132-C133, C138, C141, C144, C154-C155, C162-C163, C165-C166) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate caution. No direct peer review evaluation of these limitation statements, though peer reviewers raised similar concerns about localization (C132 mentioned in peer R1) and methodological limitations throughout their reviews.

OpenEval R14 addresses future work suggestion about 3D models and tumor microenvironment (C158) as SUPPORTED and appropriately framed. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate this future directions claim.
